title.zh: 卷五十 吳書五 妃嬪傳
title.en: Volume 50: Book of Wu 5: Biographies of Concubines and Ladies
title.raw: 卷五十 吳書五 妃嬪傳 Volume 50: Book of Wu 5: Biographies of Concubines and Ladies

sentences.zh: 吳夫人

translations.literal: Lady Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wu.

sentences.zh: 孫破虜吳夫人，吳主權母也。

translations.literal: Lady Wu, wife of Sun the Vanquisher of Foes, was the mother of Wu ruler Quan.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wu of General Sun Jian—she was the mother of Sun Quan, the Wu sovereign.

sentences.zh: 本吳人，徙錢唐，早失父母。

translations.literal: Originally a person of Wu, she moved to Qiantang and early lost both parents.
translations.idiomatic: She was born in Wu, later moved the household to Qiantang, and was orphaned while still young.

sentences.zh: 與弟景居。

translations.literal: She dwelt together with her younger brother Jing.
translations.idiomatic: She kept house with her brother Wu Jing.

sentences.zh: 孫堅聞其才貌，欲娶之。

translations.literal: Sun Jian heard of her talent and beauty and wished to marry her.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jian heard tales of her gifts and loveliness and asked for her hand.

sentences.zh: 吳氏親戚嫌堅輕狡，將拒焉，堅甚以慚恨。

translations.literal: Wu relatives disliked Jian as frivolous and crafty and were about to refuse; Jian was very ashamed and resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Her kinsmen thought Sun Jian too slick and unreliable and meant to turn him down—an insult that rankled him.

sentences.zh: 夫人謂親戚曰：「何愛一女以取禍乎？

translations.literal: The lady said to relatives, "Why cherish one daughter so as to invite disaster?
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wu told them, "Would you cling to one girl and court calamity for the whole clan?

sentences.zh: 如有不遇，命也。」

translations.literal: If there is no good match, it is fate."
translations.idiomatic: If the match proves ill-starred, that is Heaven's will."

sentences.zh: 於是遂許為婚，生四男一女。

translations.literal: Thereupon they agreed to the marriage; she bore four sons and one daughter.
translations.idiomatic: They gave their consent; she bore four sons and a daughter.

sentences.zh: 〈《搜神記》曰：初，夫人孕而夢月入其懷，既而生策。

translations.literal: 〈The Soushen ji states: At first, when the lady was pregnant she dreamed the moon entered her bosom; afterward she gave birth to Ce.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Soushen ji says that while carrying Sun Ce she dreamed the moon slipped into her breast—then bore Ce.

sentences.zh: 及權在孕，又夢日入其懷，以告堅曰：「昔妊策，夢月入我懷，今也又夢日入我懷，何也？」

translations.literal: When Quan was in the womb, again she dreamed the sun entered her bosom; she told Jian, saying, "Formerly when pregnant with Ce I dreamed the moon entered my bosom; now again I dream the sun enters my bosom—what does it mean?
translations.idiomatic: With Sun Quan in her womb she dreamed the sun had entered her breast and said to Sun Jian, "For Ce it was the moon; now it is the sun—what portent is this?"

sentences.zh: 堅曰：「日月者陰陽之精，極貴之象，吾子孫其興乎！」〉

translations.literal: Jian said, "Sun and moon are the essences of yin and yang, images of the utmost nobility; perhaps my descendants will rise!"〉
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jian answered, "Sun and moon are the twin essences of yin and yang—the badge of supreme eminence. Our line is meant to flourish!"〉

sentences.zh: 景常隨堅征伐有功，拜騎都尉。

translations.literal: Jing constantly followed Jian on campaigns with merit, was appointed Colonel of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Jing rode on every campaign beside Sun Jian, earned his share of glory, and was named Colonel of Agile Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 袁術上景領丹楊太守，討故太守周昕，遂據其郡。

translations.literal: Yuan Shu memorialized Jing to act as Grand Administrator of Danyang, to campaign against the former Grand Administrator Zhou Xin, and thereupon occupied that commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu named Wu Jing acting Grand Administrator of Danyang to oust Zhou Xin; Wu Jing held the commandery.

sentences.zh: 孫策與孫河、呂範依景，合眾共討涇縣山賊祖郎。

translations.literal: Sun Ce together with Sun He and Lü Fan relied on Jing, gathered hosts, and jointly campaigned against the mountain bandit Zu Lang of Jing county.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce, Sun He, and Lü Fan rallied to Wu Jing and joined forces against the bandit Zu Lang in Jing county.

sentences.zh: 郎敗走。

translations.literal: Lang was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Lang broke and ran.

sentences.zh: 會為劉繇所迫，景復北依術，術以為督軍中郎將，與孫賁共討樊能、於麋於橫江，又擊笮融、薛禮於秣陵。

translations.literal: It happened that he was pressed by Liu Yao; Jing again attached himself north to Shu; Shu appointed him Supervising General of the Household and together with Sun Ben campaigned against Fan Neng and Yu Mi at Hengjiang, and again struck Ze Rong and Xue Li at Moling.
translations.idiomatic: Hard pressed by Liu Yao, Wu Jing went north to Yuan Shu, who made him Supervising General of the Household; with Sun Ben he fought Fan Neng and Yu Mi at Hengjiang, then Ze Rong and Xue Li at Moling.

sentences.zh: 時策被創牛渚，降賊復反，景攻討，盡禽之。

translations.literal: At the time Ce was wounded at Niuzhu; surrendered bandits rebelled again; Jing attacked and campaigned, capturing them all.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Ce was wounded at Niuzhu and his surrendered bandits mutinied, Wu Jing struck and took every one of them.

sentences.zh: 從討劉繇，繇奔豫章，策遣景、賁到壽春報術。

translations.literal: Following the campaign against Liu Yao, Yao fled to Yuzhang; Ce dispatched Jing and Ben to Shouchun to report to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: After the drive against Liu Yao, who fled to Yuzhang, Sun Ce sent Wu Jing and Sun Ben east to brief Yuan Shu at Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 術方與劉備爭徐州，以景為為廣陵太守。

translations.literal: Shu was at that time contending with Liu Bei for Xu Province and appointed Jing as Grand Administrator of Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu, busy wrestling Xu Province from Liu Bei, named Wu Jing Grand Administrator of Guangling.

sentences.zh: 術後僭號。

translations.literal: Later Shu usurped the title.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu later declared himself emperor.

sentences.zh: 策以書喻術，術不納，便絕江津，不與通，使人告景。

translations.literal: Ce with a letter instructed Shu; Shu did not accept, then cut the Yangzi fords and did not communicate with him, sending a man to inform Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce wrote Yuan Shu a stern letter; when it was ignored, he sealed the river and sent word to Wu Jing.

sentences.zh: 景即委郡東歸，策復以景為丹揚太守。

translations.literal: Jing immediately resigned the commandery and returned east; Ce again appointed Jing as Grand Administrator of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Jing abandoned his post and came back to the east; Sun Ce restored him as Grand Administrator of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 漢遣議郎王誧

translations.literal: The Han court sent Gentleman Consultant Wang Bu—
translations.idiomatic: The Han court sent Gentleman Consultant Wang Bu—

sentences.zh: 〈音普。〉

translations.literal: 〈The gloss reads its sound as pu.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈the surname character is read "pu."〉

sentences.zh: 銜命南行，表景為揚武將軍，領郡如故。

translations.literal: Bearing orders he went south, memorialized Jing as General Who Raises Might, commanding the commandery as before.
translations.idiomatic: —bearing imperial orders south, where he cited Wu Jing as General Who Raises Might and left him in charge of the commandery.

sentences.zh: 及權少年統業，夫人助治軍國，甚有補益。

translations.literal: When Quan in youth took sole charge of the enterprise, the lady assisted in governing army and state, with much benefit.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Quan came to power while still young, Lady Wu helped him run army and state and proved a great asset.

sentences.zh: 《會稽典錄》曰：策功曹魏騰，以迕意見譴，將殺之，士大夫憂恐，計無所出。

translations.literal: The Kuaiji dian lu states: Ce had credited Cao Teng of Wei for merit; because he gave offense he was reprimanded and was about to be executed; scholar-officials were anxious and fearful, with no plan to offer.
translations.idiomatic: The Kuaiji dian lu says Sun Ce had credited Cao Teng of Wei for service; when Teng gave offense and was condemned to death, the gentry were terrified and could see no way out.

sentences.zh: 夫人乃倚大井而謂策曰：「汝新造江南，其事未集，方當優賢禮士，舍過錄功。

translations.literal: The lady then leaned against the great well and said to Ce, "You have newly built Jiangnan; the enterprise is not yet settled; you should just now honor the worthy and treat scholars with ceremony, pardon faults and record merit.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wu leaned against the great well and told Sun Ce, "You have only just begun to build Jiangnan; the work is unfinished. Now is the time to honor the worthy, treat scholars with courtesy, pardon faults, and record merit.

sentences.zh: 魏功曹在公盡規，汝今日殺之，則明日人皆叛汝。

translations.literal: The Wei merit clerk has in your service fully offered remonstrance; if you kill him today, then tomorrow everyone will rebel against you.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Teng has served you faithfully with honest counsel. Kill him today and tomorrow every man will turn against you.

sentences.zh: 吾不忍見禍之及，當先投此井中耳。」

translations.literal: I cannot bear to see calamity reach us; I shall first throw myself into this well."
translations.idiomatic: I cannot bear to see disaster fall on us—I would rather throw myself into this well first."

sentences.zh: 策大驚，遽釋騰。

translations.literal: Ce was greatly alarmed and immediately released Teng.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce was shaken and released Cao Teng at once.

sentences.zh: 夫人智略權譎，類皆如此。

translations.literal: The lady's wisdom, stratagem, and resourcefulness were all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wu's shrewd counsel was often of this sort.

sentences.zh: 建安七年，臨薨，引見張昭等，屬以後事，合葬高陵。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Jian'an, as she neared death, she summoned Zhang Zhao and others, entrusted them with later affairs, and was buried together at Gaoling.
translations.idiomatic: In Jian'an 7, on her deathbed she summoned Zhang Zhao and others to entrust them with affairs after her death; she was buried with Sun Jian at Gaoling.

sentences.zh: 《志林》曰：按會稽貢舉簿，建安十二年到十三年闕，無舉者，云府君遭憂，此則吳后以十二年薨也。

translations.literal: The Zhi lin states: According to the Kuaiji tribute-and-recommendation register, from the twelfth to the thirteenth year of Jian'an there is a gap with no recommendees; it says the prefect suffered bereavement—this shows the Wu empress died in the twelfth year.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhi lin notes that Kuaiji's recommendation register has no entries for Jian'an 12–13, citing the prefect's bereavement—evidence that Lady Wu died in Jian'an 12.

sentences.zh: 八年九年皆有貢舉，斯甚分明。

translations.literal: The eighth and ninth years both have tribute recommendations; this is very clear.
translations.idiomatic: Recommendations resume in Jian'an 8 and 9, which makes the dating plain.

sentences.zh: 八年，景卒宮，子奮授兵為將，封新亭侯，卒。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Jing died at the palace; his son Fen was given troops as a general, enfeoffed as Marquis of Xinting, and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of the reign Wu Jing died at court; his son Wu Fen took command, became Marquis of Xinting, and predeceased his father.

sentences.zh: 〈《吳書》曰：權徵荊州，拜奮吳郡都督，以鎮東方。

translations.literal: 〈The Wu shu states: When Quan campaigned to Jing Province, he appointed Fen as Wu commandery Area Commander to guard the east.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Wu shu notes that when Sun Quan marched on Jingzhou he made Wu Fen area commander of Wu commandery to hold the eastern flank.

sentences.zh: 《吳書》曰：祺與張溫、顧譚友善，權令關平辭訟事。〉

translations.literal: The Wu shu states: Qi was on friendly terms with Zhang Wen and Gu Tan; Quan had him oversee the clearing of lawsuits.〉
translations.idiomatic: The same text adds that Wu Qi befriended Zhang Wen and Gu Tan, and Sun Quan set him to straighten out the docket.〉

sentences.zh: 子安嗣，安坐黨魯王霸死。

translations.literal: His son An succeeded; An died because of implication with the Prince of Lu, Ba.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Fen's heir Wu An fell with the Prince of Lu, Sun Ba, and was put to death.

sentences.zh: 奮弟祺嗣，封都亭侯，卒。

translations.literal: Fen's younger brother Qi succeeded, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Duting, and died.
translations.idiomatic: The younger brother Wu Qi inherited the fief as Marquis of Duting and died without long tenure.

sentences.zh: 子纂嗣。

translations.literal: His son Zuan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wu Zuan carried on the title.

sentences.zh: 纂妻即滕胤女也，胤被誅，竝遇害。

translations.literal: Zuan's wife was the daughter of Teng Yin; when Yin was executed, together they met harm.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zuan had married Teng Yin's daughter; when Teng Yin was executed, husband and wife perished together.

sentences.zh: 謝夫人

translations.literal: Lady Xie.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xie.

sentences.zh: 吳主權謝夫人，會稽山陰人也。

translations.literal: Lady Xie, consort of Wu ruler Quan, was a native of Shanyin in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xie of Sun Quan came from Shanyin in Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 父煚，漢尚書郎、徐令。

translations.literal: Her father Jiong was a Gentleman of the Masters of Writing of Han and magistrate of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Xie Jiong had served the Han court as a Masters of Writing gentleman and as magistrate of Xu.

sentences.zh: 〈煚子承撰《後漢書》，稱煚幼以仁孝為行，明達有令才。

translations.literal: 〈Jiong's son Cheng wrote the Hou Han shu, stating Jiong in youth took humane filial conduct as his practice, was enlightened and reached, and had fine talent.
translations.idiomatic: 〈Their son Xie Cheng, author of the Hou Han shu, wrote that Xie Jiong was known from boyhood for humane piety, clear judgment, and outstanding gifts.

sentences.zh: 煚弟貞，履蹈法度，篤學尚義，舉孝廉，建昌長，卒官。〉

translations.literal: Jiong's younger brother Zhen trod in statutes and law, loved learning and honored righteousness, was recommended as Filial and Incorrupt, was chief of Jianchang, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Xie Zhen walked the straight path of the code, loved learning and honor, rose as Filial and Incorrupt, and died in office as chief of Jianchang.

sentences.zh: 權母吳，為權聘以為妃，愛幸有寵。

translations.literal: Quan's mother Wu, for Quan, engaged her to be consort; she was loved and favored and had favor.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wu betrothed her to Sun Quan as principal consort, and she basked in his favor.

sentences.zh: 後權納姑孫徐氏，欲令謝下之，謝不肯，由是失志。

translations.literal: Later Quan took in marriage his cousin on the distaff side, Lady Xu of the Sun clan, and wished to make Xie yield place beneath her; Xie refused; therefore she lost aspiration.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Quan married his maternal cousin Lady Xu and expected Lady Xie to step aside, she refused and fell from grace.

sentences.zh: 早卒。

translations.literal: She died early.
translations.idiomatic: She died young.

sentences.zh: 後十餘年，弟承拜五官郎中，稍遷長沙東部都尉、武陵太守，撰《後漢書》百餘卷。

translations.literal: After more than ten years, younger brother Cheng was appointed Gentlemen of the Five Offices, gradually promoted to Eastern Division Commandant of Changsha and Grand Administrator of Wuling, and wrote the Hou Han shu in more than one hundred scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: A decade later her brother Xie Cheng rose to Gentlemen of the Five Offices, then Eastern Division commandant at Changsha and Grand Administrator of Wuling, and composed the Hou Han shu in over a hundred fascicles.

sentences.zh: 〈《會稽典錄》曰：承字偉平，博學洽聞，嘗所知見，終身不忘。

translations.literal: 〈The Kuaiji dian lu states: Cheng, courtesy name Weiping, was broadly learned and well informed; what he once saw or knew he never forgot to the end of life.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Kuaiji dian lu calls Xie Cheng styled Weiping, encyclopedic in memory and learning.

sentences.zh: 子崇揚威將軍，崇弟勗吳郡太守，竝知名。〉

translations.literal: His son Chong was General Who Raises Might; Chong's younger brother Xu was Grand Administrator of Wu commandery; both were renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Chong became General Who Raises Might, Xie Xu Grand Administrator of Wu—both names the age remembered.

sentences.zh: 徐夫人

translations.literal: Lady Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xu.

sentences.zh: 吳主權徐夫人，吳郡富春人也。

translations.literal: Lady Xu, consort of Wu ruler Quan, was a native of Fuchun in Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xu of Sun Quan was a daughter of Fuchun in Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖父真，與權父堅相親，堅以妹妻真，生琨。

translations.literal: Her grandfather Zhen was intimate with Quan's father Jian; Jian gave his younger sister in marriage to Zhen, who begot Kun.
translations.idiomatic: Her grandfather Xu Zhen was close to Sun Jian, who married him a sister; they had Xu Kun.

sentences.zh: 琨少仕州郡，漢末擾亂，去吏，隨堅征伐有功，拜偏將軍。

translations.literal: Kun in youth served the province and commandery; at the end of Han there was turmoil; he left clerical office, followed Jian on campaigns with merit, was appointed Lieutenant General.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Kun began in local office, quit at the Han collapse, followed Sun Jian with distinction, and won the rank of Lieutenant General.

sentences.zh: 堅薨，隨孫策討樊能、於糜等於橫江，擊張英於當利口。

translations.literal: When Jian died, he followed Sun Ce to campaign against Fan Neng, Yu Mi, and others at Hengjiang, and struck Zhang Ying at Danglikou.
translations.idiomatic: After Sun Jian's death he joined Sun Ce against Fan Neng and Yu Mi at Hengjiang and Zhang Ying at Danglikou.

sentences.zh: 而船少，欲駐軍更求。

translations.literal: But boats were few; he wished to halt the army and seek more.
translations.idiomatic: Boats were scarce; he wanted to halt and fetch more craft.

sentences.zh: 琨母時在軍中，謂琨曰：「恐州家多發水軍來逆人，則不利矣，如何可駐邪？

translations.literal: Kun's mother was at that time in the army and said to Kun, "I fear the provincial authorities will send many water forces to oppose men; then it will not be advantageous—how can we halt?
translations.idiomatic: His mother, still with the host, warned him, "If the enemy throws a fleet against us, stopping here will be fatal—how can you wait?

sentences.zh: 宜伐蘆葦以為泭，佐船渡軍。」

translations.literal: It is fitting to cut reeds to make rafts, to assist the boats in ferrying the army."
translations.idiomatic: Cut reeds into floats and ferry the army across on them."

sentences.zh: 〈泭音敷。

translations.literal: 〈The note gives fu as the reading.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈The note gives fu as the reading.〉

sentences.zh: 郭璞注《方言》曰：「泭，水中簰也。」〉

translations.literal: Guo Pu's commentary on the Fang yan states, "Fu is a raft on the water."〉
translations.idiomatic: In his Fang yan commentary Guo Pu glosses the word as "fu," meaning a raft used on the water.〉

sentences.zh: 琨具啟策，策即行之。

translations.literal: Kun fully reported to Ce; Ce immediately carried it out.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Kun laid the plan before Sun Ce, who adopted it at once.

sentences.zh: 眾悉俱濟，遂破英，擊走笮融、劉繇，事業克定。

translations.literal: The host all crossed together; thereupon they defeated Ying, struck and drove away Ze Rong and Liu Yao, and the enterprise was settled.
translations.idiomatic: The whole force crossed, broke Zhang Ying, and sent Ze Rong and Liu Yao flying—the southeast was theirs.

sentences.zh: 策表琨領丹楊太守，會吳景委廣陵來東，復為丹楊守。

translations.literal: Ce memorialized Kun to act as Grand Administrator of Danyang; it happened that Wu Jing resigned Guangling and came east, and again became Danyang defender.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce cited Xu Kun as acting Grand Administrator of Danyang until Wu Jing returned from Guangling and resumed that post.

sentences.zh: 〈《江表傳》曰：初，袁術遣從弟胤為丹楊，策令琨討而代之。

translations.literal: 〈The Jiang biao zhuan states: At first Yuan Shu dispatched his cousin Yin as Danyang; Ce ordered Kun to campaign against him and replace him.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Jiang biao zhuan says Yuan Shu first planted his cousin in Danyang until Sun Ce sent Xu Kun to oust him.

sentences.zh: 會景還，以景前在

translations.literal: It happened that Jing returned; because Jing previously in
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Jing came back, Sun Quan reasoned that Wu Jing had once served in

translations.literal: (office)
translations.idiomatic: office

sentences.zh: 丹楊，寬仁得眾，吏民所思，而琨手下兵多，策嫌其太重，且方攻伐，宜得琨眾，乃復用景，召琨還吳。〉

translations.literal: Danyang had been kind and benevolent and won the people, whom clerks and commoners longed for, while Kun's subordinate troops were many; Ce disliked it as too weighty, and moreover was just then attacking; it was fitting to obtain Kun's host; therefore he again employed Jing, summoned Kun back to Wu.〉
translations.idiomatic: Danyang with such kindness that the people missed him, while Xu Kun's following had grown unwieldy for an army on the march—so Sun Ce put Wu Jing back in charge and recalled Xu Kun to Wu.〉

sentences.zh: 琨以督軍中郎將領兵，從破廬江太守李術，封廣德侯，遷平虜將軍。

translations.literal: Kun as Supervising General of the Household led troops, followed in breaking Grand Administrator of Lujiang Li Shu, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Guangde, promoted to General Who Pacifies Captives.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Kun led troops as Supervising General of the Household, helped crush Li Shu at Lujiang, became Marquis of Guangde, and rose to General Who Pacifies Captives.

sentences.zh: 後從討黃祖，中流矢卒。

translations.literal: Later following the campaign against Huang Zu, in midstream he was struck by a stray arrow and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was killed by a stray shaft while campaigning against Huang Zu.

sentences.zh: 琨生夫人，初適同郡陸尚。

translations.literal: Kun begot the lady; at first she was married to Lu Shang of the same commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Kun's daughter had first married Lu Shang of Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 尚卒，極為討虜將軍在吳，聘以為妃，使母養子登。

translations.literal: When Shang died, Quan, being General Who Punishes Captives at Wu, engaged her to be consort, and had his mother nurture the son Deng.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Shang died, Sun Quan—then General Who Punishes Captives at Wu—took her as consort and had Lady Wu raise his heir Sun Deng.

sentences.zh: 後權遷移，以夫人妒忌，廢處吳。

translations.literal: Later when Quan moved his seat, because the lady was jealous, he deposed her and placed her at Wu.
translations.idiomatic: After he shifted his capital he banished her to Wu for jealousy.

sentences.zh: 積十餘年，權為吳王及即尊號，登為太子，群臣請立夫人為后，權意在步氏，卒不許。

translations.literal: Accumulating more than ten years, when Quan became King of Wu and ascended the exalted title, Deng became heir apparent; the host of ministers requested to establish the lady as empress; Quan's intention was on the Bu clan, and in the end he did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: For ten years she languished while Sun Quan became king and then emperor and Sun Deng crown prince; ministers begged to make her empress, but his heart was set on Lady Bu and he refused.

sentences.zh: 後以疾卒。

translations.literal: Later she died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: She died of illness in confinement.

sentences.zh: 兄矯，嗣父琨侯，討平山越，拜偏將軍，先夫人卒，無子。

translations.literal: Elder brother Jiao succeeded to father's Marquis Kun title, campaigned to pacify the mountain Yue, was appointed Lieutenant General, died before the lady, without sons.
translations.idiomatic: Her brother Xu Jiao inherited the marquisate, subdued the mountain Yue as Lieutenant General, and died childless before she did.

sentences.zh: 弟祚襲封，亦以戰功至

translations.literal: Younger brother Zuo inherited the enfeoffment, also by battle merit reached
translations.idiomatic: Brother Xu Zuo inherited the title and rose through merit to

translations.literal: (at)
translations.idiomatic: become

sentences.zh: 蕪湖督、平魏將軍。

translations.literal: Wuhu Area Commander, General Who Pacifies Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Wuhu area commander and General Who Pacifies Wei.

sentences.zh: 步夫人

translations.literal: Lady Bu.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Bu.

sentences.zh: 吳主權步夫人，臨淮淮陰人也。

translations.literal: Lady Bu, consort of Wu ruler Quan, was a native of Huaiyin in Linhuai.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Bu of Sun Quan hailed from Huaiyin in Linhuai.

sentences.zh: 與丞相騭同族。

translations.literal: She was of the same clan as Chancellor Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: She belonged to the same lineage as Chancellor Bu Zhi.

sentences.zh: 漢末，其母攜將徙廬江，廬江為孫策所破，皆東渡江，以美麗得幸於權，寵冠後庭。

translations.literal: At the end of Han, her mother led and moved to Lujiang; Lujiang was broken by Sun Ce; all crossed the river east; by beauty she obtained favor with Quan, favor crowning the rear palace.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Han her mother fled with her to Lujiang; Sun Ce's storm drove them east across the Yangzi, where her beauty won Sun Quan's heart above every other woman in the harem.

sentences.zh: 生二女，長曰魯班，字大虎，前配周瑜子循，後配全琮。

translations.literal: She bore two daughters; the elder was called Luban, courtesy name Dahu, first matched to Zhou Yu's son Xun, afterward matched to Quan Zong.
translations.idiomatic: She bore two daughters: the elder, Sun Luban—styled Dahu—first wed Zhou Yu's son Zhou Xun, later Quan Zong.

sentences.zh: 少曰魯育，字小虎，前配朱據，後配劉纂。

translations.literal: The younger was called Luyu, courtesy name Xiaohu, first matched to Zhu Ju, afterward matched to Liu Zuan.
translations.idiomatic: The younger, Sun Luyu—styled Xiaohu—first wed Zhu Ju, then Liu Zuan.

sentences.zh: 〈《吳曆》曰：纂先尚權中女，早卒，故又以小虎為繼室。〉

translations.literal: 〈The Wu li states: Zuan had first married Quan's middle daughter; she died early; therefore he took Xiaohu as successor wife.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Wu li notes Liu Zuan had earlier married Sun Quan's middle daughter, who died young, so Xiaohu became his second wife.

sentences.zh: 夫人性不妒忌，多所推近，故久見愛待。

translations.literal: The lady by nature was not jealous, many she drew near and promoted; therefore for long she was loved and treated kindly.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Bu was free of jealousy, lifted up rivals, and so kept the sovereign's affection year after year.

sentences.zh: 權為王及帝，意欲以為后，而群臣議在徐氏，權依違者十餘年，然宮內皆稱皇后，親戚上疏稱中宮。

translations.literal: When Quan became king and emperor, his intention wished to make her empress, but the host of ministers deliberated that it should be the Xu clan; Quan vacillated for more than ten years, yet within the palace all called her empress, and relatives in memorials called her Central Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan meant to crown her empress, yet ministers insisted the honor belonged to Lady Xu; he wavered a decade while the harem already hailed her as empress and kin addressed her as Central Palace.

sentences.zh: 及薨，臣下緣權指，請追正名號，乃贈印綬，策命曰：

translations.literal: When she died, inferiors following Quan's intent requested to rectify the title posthumously; thereupon they presented seals and ribbons, the patent reading:
translations.idiomatic: At her death his courtiers, reading his wishes, asked to set her title straight; seals and patent were issued:

sentences.zh: 惟赤烏元年閏月戊子，皇帝曰：嗚呼皇后，惟后佐命，共承天地。

translations.literal: Only in the intercalary month wuzi of the first year of Chiwu, the Emperor said: Alas, Empress; only you assisted the mandate, together receiving Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Chiwu 1, intercalary month, day wuzi: "Alas, my queen—you shared the Mandate and bore Heaven and Earth with me."

sentences.zh: 虔恭夙夜，與朕均勞。

translations.literal: Reverent and respectful morning and night, together with Us sharing toil.
translations.idiomatic: Night and day you kept the inner quarters in order and bore the burden at my side.

sentences.zh: 內教修整，禮義不愆。

translations.literal: Inner instruction was set in order; ritual and righteousness were not transgressed.
translations.idiomatic: You taught the household propriety and never strayed from the rites.

sentences.zh: 寬容慈惠，有淑懿之德。

translations.literal: Broad, tolerant, kind, and gracious—you had virtuous and excellent virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Your mercy and patience were the very mold of womanly virtue.

sentences.zh: 民臣懸望，遠近歸心。

translations.literal: The people and ministers hung in hope; far and near returned heart.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and commoners looked to you; loyalties gathered from every quarter.

sentences.zh: 朕以世難未夷，大統未一，緣后雅志，每懷謙損。

translations.literal: We, because the age's troubles were not yet pacified, the great unity not yet one, following the queen's refined intent, always cherished modest yielding.
translations.idiomatic: While the realm stayed divided I deferred, honoring your own wish to remain humble.

sentences.zh: 是以於時未授名號，亦必謂后降年有永，永與朕躬對揚天休。

translations.literal: Therefore at that time We did not confer title and name, also surely thinking the queen's declining years would be long, forever with Our person answering and raising Heaven's blessing.
translations.idiomatic: So I withheld the formal title, sure we would have years yet to proclaim your glory together.

sentences.zh: 不寤奄忽，大命近止。

translations.literal: We did not awake to your sudden going; the great mandate draws near its stop.
translations.idiomatic: Instead death took you in a breath—the great summons has come.

sentences.zh: 朕恨本意不早昭顯，傷后殂逝，不終天祿。

translations.literal: We hate that Our original intent did not early shine clear; grieving the queen's passing, she did not finish Heaven's blessing.
translations.idiomatic: I bitterly regret I never proclaimed you empress in life; you left before Heaven's full favor was spent.

sentences.zh: 愍悼之至，痛於厥心。

translations.literal: The pity and grief are utmost; pain is in Our heart.
translations.idiomatic: My sorrow is bottomless; the ache sits in my breast.

sentences.zh: 今使使持節丞相

translations.literal: Now We send the bearer of credentials, Chancellor
translations.idiomatic: Now I dispatch the credential-bearing Chancellor

sentences.zh: （醴陵亭侯雍）

translations.literal: (Marquis of Liling Precinct, Yong [Gu Yong])
translations.idiomatic: (Gu Yong, Marquis of Liling precinct)

sentences.zh: 奉策授號，配食先后。

translations.literal: to receive the patent and confer title, to share sacrifice with the former queens.
translations.idiomatic: to invest you posthumously and set your tablet beside my forebears' consorts.

sentences.zh: 魂而有靈，嘉其寵榮。

translations.literal: If the soul has awareness, rejoice in this favor and glory.
translations.idiomatic: If spirit endures, take joy in this crowning honor.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼哀哉！

translations.literal: Alas, how sad!
translations.idiomatic: Alas—how we mourn!

sentences.zh: 葬於蔣陵。

translations.literal: She was buried at Jiang Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: She was laid to rest at Jiang Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 琅邪王夫人

translations.literal: Lady Wang of Langye.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wang of Langye.

sentences.zh: 吳主權王夫人，琅邪人也。

translations.literal: Lady Wang, consort of Wu ruler Quan, was a native of Langye.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wang of Sun Quan came from Langye.

sentences.zh: 〈《吳書》曰：夫人父名盧九。〉

translations.literal: 〈The Wu shu states: The lady's father's name was Lu Jiu.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Wu shu names her father Lu Jiu.〉

sentences.zh: 夫人以選入宮，黃武中得幸，生

translations.literal: The lady by selection entered the palace; in the Huangwu period obtained favor and gave birth to
translations.idiomatic: Drafted into the palace, she won favor during the Huangwu years and bore

translations.literal: (Sun)
translations.idiomatic: the house of Sun—

sentences.zh: 和，寵次步氏。

translations.literal: He; favor was second to the Bu clan.
translations.idiomatic: Sun He, enjoying favor second only to Lady Bu.

sentences.zh: 步氏薨後，和立為太子，權將立夫人為后，而全公主素憎夫人，稍稍譖毀。

translations.literal: After Lady Bu died, He was established as heir apparent; Quan was about to establish the lady as empress, but the Princess of Quan had long hated the lady, gradually slandering and destroying her.
translations.idiomatic: When Lady Bu died and Sun He became heir, Sun Quan meant to make this Lady Wang empress; Princess Quan (Sun Luban), who had always detested her, whispered slander until the match collapsed.

sentences.zh: 及權寢疾。

translations.literal: When Quan lay gravely ill.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan sank into mortal illness.

sentences.zh: 言有喜色，由是權深責怒，以憂死。

translations.literal: She showed a joyful expression in speaking; whereupon Quan deeply blamed and was angry, and she died of grief.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wang's face lit with ill-concealed hope; Sun Quan saw it, raged at her disloyalty, and she died of grief and fear.

sentences.zh: 和子皓立，追尊夫人曰大懿皇后，封三弟皆列侯。

translations.literal: When He's son Hao succeeded, he posthumously honored the lady as Grand Consummate Empress, enfeoffing three younger brothers as full marquises.
translations.idiomatic: Sun He's son Sun Hao later canonized her as Grand Consummate Empress and ennobled her three brothers as full marquises.

sentences.zh: 南陽王夫人

translations.literal: Lady Wang of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wang of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 吳主權王夫人，南陽人也。

translations.literal: Lady Wang, consort of Wu ruler Quan, was a native of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Nanyang Lady Wang was another of Sun Quan's consorts.

sentences.zh: 以選人宮，嘉禾中得幸，生

translations.literal: By selection she entered the palace; in the Jiahe period obtained favor and gave birth to
translations.idiomatic: Chosen for the harem, she won favor in the Jiahe era and bore

translations.literal: (Sun)
translations.idiomatic: the child was

sentences.zh: 休。

translations.literal: Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiu.

sentences.zh: 及和為太子，和母貴重，諸姬有寵者，皆出居外。

translations.literal: When He was heir apparent, He's mother was noble and weighty; concubines who had favor all went out to dwell outside.
translations.idiomatic: Once Sun He was heir, his mother's faction dominated; favored concubines were packed off to residences outside the palace.

sentences.zh: 夫人出公安，卒，因葬焉。

translations.literal: The lady went out to Gong'an, died, and was therefore buried there.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wang was sent to Gong'an, where she died and was buried.

sentences.zh: 休即位，遣使追尊曰敬懷皇后，改葬敬陵。

translations.literal: When Xiu ascended the throne, he dispatched envoys to posthumously honor her as Empress Jinghuai, and changed burial to Jing Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Xiu took the throne he posthumously named her Empress Jinghuai and moved her grave to the Jing mausoleum complex.

sentences.zh: 王氏無後，封同母弟文雍為亭侯。

translations.literal: The Wang clan had no posterity; he enfeoffed her uterine younger brother Wen Yong as precinct marquis.
translations.idiomatic: With no Wang heir to honor, he enfeoffed her half-brother Wang Wenyong as a precinct marquis.

sentences.zh: 潘夫人

translations.literal: Lady Pan.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Pan.

sentences.zh: 吳主權潘夫人，會稽句章人也。

translations.literal: Lady Pan, consort of Wu ruler Quan, was a native of Gouzhang in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Pan of Sun Quan came from Gouzhang in Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 父為吏，坐法死。

translations.literal: Her father was a clerk; because of violating the law he died.
translations.idiomatic: Her father was a petty clerk who was executed for breaking the law.

sentences.zh: 夫人與姊俱輸織室，權見而異之，召充後宮。

translations.literal: The lady together with her elder sister both were sent to the weaving room; Quan saw and thought her unusual, summoned her to fill the rear palace.
translations.idiomatic: She and her sister were consigned to the imperial weaving house until Sun Quan noticed her, struck by her looks, and took her into the harem.

sentences.zh: 得幸有娠，夢有以龍頭授己者，己以蔽膝受之，遂生

translations.literal: Obtaining favor she was pregnant; she dreamed someone gave her a dragon head; she received it with the apron; thereupon gave birth to
translations.idiomatic: While carrying a royal child she dreamed a hand offered her a dragon's head, which she caught in her skirt—then she bore

translations.literal: (Sun)
translations.idiomatic: Sun

sentences.zh: 亮。

translations.literal: Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Liang.

sentences.zh: 赤烏十三年，亮立為太子，請出嫁夫人之姊，權聽許之。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Chiwu, Liang was established as heir apparent; he requested to marry out the lady's elder sister; Quan listened and granted.
translations.idiomatic: In Chiwu 13 Sun Liang was named heir; he asked leave to marry out Lady Pan's elder sister, and Sun Quan agreed.

sentences.zh: 明年，立夫人為皇后。

translations.literal: The next year, he established the lady as empress.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he raised Lady Pan to empress.

sentences.zh: 性險妒容媚，自始至卒，譖害袁夫人等甚眾。

translations.literal: By nature treacherous, jealous, and flattering, from first to death she slandered and harmed Lady Yuan and others in great number.
translations.idiomatic: She was vicious, jealous, and skilled at flattery, and spent her years in the palace destroying rivals such as Lady Yuan.

sentences.zh: 〈《吳錄》曰：袁夫人者，袁術女也，有節行而無子。

translations.literal: 〈The Wu lu states: Lady Yuan was Yuan Shu's daughter; she had integrity and conduct but no sons.
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Wu lu identifies Lady Yuan as Yuan Shu's daughter—virtuous and childless.

sentences.zh: 權數以諸姬子與養之，輒不育。

translations.literal: Quan several times gave her the sons of various concubines to raise; always they did not thrive.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan repeatedly gave her other women's infants to raise; none survived.

sentences.zh: 及步夫人薨，權欲立之。

translations.literal: When Lady Bu died, Quan wished to establish her.
translations.idiomatic: After Lady Bu's death Sun Quan meant to make Lady Yuan empress.

sentences.zh: 夫人自以無子，固辭不受。〉

translations.literal: The lady considered herself without sons, firmly declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing she had borne no heir, Lady Yuan refused the crown outright.

sentences.zh: 權不豫，夫人使問中書令孫弘呂后專制故事。

translations.literal: When Quan was indisposed, the lady sent to ask Director of the Palace Writers Sun Hong for precedents of Empress Lü's exclusive rule.
translations.idiomatic: While Sun Quan lay ill, Lady Pan sent to Sun Hong, Director of the Palace Writers, for stories of how Empress Lü seized sole power.

sentences.zh: 侍疾疲勞，因以羸疾，諸宮人伺其昏臥，共縊殺之，託言中惡。

translations.literal: Attending illness she was weary; therefore she had a wasting illness; various palace women waited until she was drowsily asleep, together strangled her to death, pretending sudden illness.
translations.idiomatic: Nursing him left her exhausted and frail; a pack of maids waited until she slept, then garroted her and blamed a sudden seizure.

sentences.zh: 後事洩，坐死者六七人。

translations.literal: Later the affair leaked; six or seven persons for it died.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot surfaced, six or seven women paid with their lives.

sentences.zh: 權尋薨，合葬蔣陵。

translations.literal: Quan soon after died; joint burial at Jiang Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan died soon after; she was interred with him at Jiang Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 孫亮即位，以夫人姊婿譚紹為騎都尉，授兵。

translations.literal: When Sun Liang succeeded, he appointed Tan Shao, husband of the lady's elder sister, as Colonel of Agile Cavalry and gave troops.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Liang named Tan Shao—Lady Pan's brother-in-law—Colonel of Agile Cavalry with a command.

sentences.zh: 亮廢，紹與家屬送本部廬陵。

translations.literal: When Liang was deposed, Shao together with family members was sent to their native commandery Luling.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Liang was cast down, Tan Shao and his kin were banished to their home commandery of Luling.

sentences.zh: 全夫人

translations.literal: Lady Quan.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Quan.

sentences.zh: 孫亮全夫人，全尚女也。

translations.literal: Sun Liang's Lady Quan was the daughter of Quan Shang.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Liang's empress was Quan Shang's daughter.

translations.literal: (Shang)
translations.idiomatic: Quan Shang—

sentences.zh: 從祖母公主愛之，每進見輒與俱。

translations.literal: Her father's aunt the princess loved her; each time advancing to audience always went together with her.
translations.idiomatic: —was doted on by her grandaunt Princess Quan, who insisted on escorting her to every audience.

sentences.zh: 及潘夫人母子有寵，全主自以與孫和母有隙，乃勸權為潘氏男亮納夫人，亮遂為嗣。

translations.literal: When Lady Pan and her son had favor, the Princess of Quan considered herself at odds with Sun He's mother, therefore urged Quan to take in the Lady Quan for Pan's son Liang; Liang thereupon became successor.
translations.idiomatic: Once Lady Pan and Sun Liang rose, Princess Quan—feuding with Sun He's mother—talked Sun Quan into marrying Quan Shang's daughter to young Liang, making Liang heir.

sentences.zh: 夫人立為皇后，以尚為城門校尉，封都亭侯，代滕胤為太常、衛將軍，進封永平侯，錄尚書事。

translations.literal: The lady was established as empress; Shang was made Colonel of the City Gates, enfeoffed as Marquis of Duting, replaced Teng Yin as Grand Master of Ceremonies and Guards General, advanced enfeoffment to Marquis of Yongping, recorded Masters of Writing affairs.
translations.idiomatic: She became empress; Quan Shang became Colonel of the City Gates and Marquis of Duting, then Grand Master of Ceremonies and Guards General, Marquis of Yongping, with oversight of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時全氏侯有五人，並典兵馬。

translations.literal: At the time there were five persons of the Quan surname enfeoffed as marquises, together commanding military horse.
translations.idiomatic: Five Quan kinsmen held marquisates and field commands at once.

sentences.zh: 其餘為侍郎、騎都尉，宿衛左右，自吳興，外戚貴盛莫及。

translations.literal: The rest were Gentlemen Consultants, Colonels of Agile Cavalry, guarding left and right of the bedchamber; from Wu's rise, outside affines' noble flourishing none matched.
translations.idiomatic: The rest held gentleman and colonel posts and stood night watch at court; since Wu first rose, no other consort clan had matched their blaze of power.

sentences.zh: 及魏大將諸葛誕以壽春來附，而全懌、全端、全禕、全儀等並因此際降魏。

translations.literal: When Wei great general Zhuge Dan came to attach from Shouchun, Quan Yi, Quan Duan, Quan Yi, and Quan Yi, among others, at this juncture surrendered to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei general Zhuge Dan came over from Shouchun, Quan Yi, Quan Duan, Quan Yi, Quan Yi, and the rest of that clan used the turmoil to defect to Wei.

sentences.zh: 全熙謀洩見殺，由是諸全衰弱。

translations.literal: Quan Xi's plot leaked and he was seen and killed; whereby the various Quan became weak.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Xi's conspiracy surfaced and he was executed, and the Quan clan collapsed overnight.

sentences.zh: 會孫綝廢亮為會稽王，後又黜為候官侯。

translations.literal: It happened that Sun Chen deposed Liang as Prince of Kuaiji, later again demoted him to Marquis of Houguan.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Chen first demoted Sun Liang to Prince of Kuaiji, then reduced him again to Marquis of Houguan.

sentences.zh: 夫人隨之國，居候官，尚將家屬徙零陵，追見殺。

translations.literal: The lady followed him to the state, dwelt at Houguan; Shang led family members moved toward Lingling, was pursued and killed.
translations.idiomatic: The empress followed him into exile at Houguan; Quan Shang shepherded his kin toward Lingling but was overtaken and cut down.

sentences.zh: 〈《吳錄》曰：亮妻惠解有容色，居候官，吳平乃歸，永寧中卒。〉

translations.literal: 〈The Wu lu states: Liang's wife was perceptive and fair of face; dwelling at Houguan, when Wu was pacified she returned, and died in the Yongning period.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Wu lu records that Sun Liang's wife was quick-witted and lovely; she remained at Houguan until Jin conquered Wu, then returned home and died in the Yongning era.〉

sentences.zh: 朱夫人

translations.literal: Lady Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhu.

sentences.zh: 孫休朱夫人，朱據女，休姊公主所生也。

translations.literal: Sun Xiu's Lady Zhu was the daughter of Zhu Ju, born to Xiu's elder sister the princess.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiu's consort Lady Zhu was Zhu Ju's daughter, born to Xiu's elder sister the princess.

sentences.zh: 臣松之以為休妻其甥，事同漢惠。

translations.literal: Your servant Songzhi considers that Xiu married his nephew's daughter, the case being the same as Emperor Hui of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi notes that Sun Xiu married his niece—parallel to Emperor Hui of Han.

sentences.zh: 荀悅譏之已當，故不復廣言。

translations.literal: Xun Yue's censure was already apt; therefore I do not expand further.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Yue's censure was apt enough, so I say no more.

sentences.zh: 赤烏末，權為休納以為妃。

translations.literal: At the end of Chiwu, Quan took her in marriage for Xiu to be consort.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Chiwu era Sun Quan betrothed her to Sun Xiu as consort.

sentences.zh: 休為琅邪王，隨居丹楊。

translations.literal: Xiu was Prince of Langye and dwelt accordingly in Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiu was Prince of Langye and lived with her in Danyang.

sentences.zh: 建興中，孫峻專政，公族皆患之。

translations.literal: In the Jianxing period Sun Jun monopolized government; the imperial clan all feared it.
translations.idiomatic: During Jianxing Sun Jun seized power, and every member of the imperial house feared him.

sentences.zh: 全尚妻即峻姊。

translations.literal: Quan Shang's wife was Jun's elder sister.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Shang had married Jun's elder sister.

sentences.zh: 故惟全主祐焉。

translations.literal: Therefore only the Princess of Quan protected her.
translations.idiomatic: Only Princess Quan (Sun Luban) therefore shielded Lady Zhu.

sentences.zh: 初，孫和為太子時，全主譖害王夫人，欲廢太子，立魯王，朱主不聽，由是有隙。

translations.literal: At first, when Sun He was heir apparent, the Princess of Quan slandered Lady Wang, wishing to depose the heir and establish the Prince of Lu; Lady Zhu would not listen, and from this there was a rift.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun He was crown prince, Princess Quan slandered Lady Wang to depose the heir and elevate the Prince of Lu; Lady Zhu refused to go along, and a feud opened between them.

sentences.zh: 五鳳中，孫儀謀殺峻，事覺被誅。

translations.literal: In the Wufeng period Sun Yi plotted to kill Jun; the affair was discovered and he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: In Wufeng Sun Yi plotted to kill Sun Jun; the plot was exposed and he was executed.

sentences.zh: 全主因言朱主與儀同謀，峻枉殺朱主。

translations.literal: The Princess of Quan thereupon said Lady Zhu had conspired with Yi; Jun wrongly killed Lady Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Quan then claimed Lady Zhu had conspired with Sun Yi, and Jun had Lady Zhu executed on false grounds.

sentences.zh: 休懼，遣夫人還建業，執手泣別。

translations.literal: Xiu was afraid and sent the lady back to Jianye, clasping hands and weeping in parting.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Sun Xiu sent Lady Zhu back to Jianye, weeping as they clasped hands in farewell.

sentences.zh: 既至，峻遣還休。

translations.literal: When she arrived, Jun sent her back to Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: Once she reached the capital, Jun sent her back to Sun Xiu.

sentences.zh: 太平中，孫亮知朱主為全主所害，問朱主死意？

translations.literal: In the Taiping period Sun Liang learned Lady Zhu had been harmed by the Princess of Quan and asked about the circumstances of Lady Zhu's death.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiping Sun Liang learned Princess Quan had engineered Lady Zhu's death and questioned her about it.

sentences.zh: 全主懼曰：「我實不知，皆據二子熊、損所白。」

translations.literal: The Princess of Quan, afraid, said, "I truly did not know; it was all reported by Ju's two sons Xiong and Sun."
translations.idiomatic: Princess Quan, terrified, said, "I truly knew nothing—it all came from Zhu Ju's sons Xiong and Sun."

sentences.zh: 亮殺熊、損。

translations.literal: Liang killed Xiong and Sun.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Liang had Zhu Xiong and Zhu Sun executed.

sentences.zh: 損妻是峻妹也，孫綝益忌亮，遂廢亮，立休。

translations.literal: Sun's wife was Jun's younger sister; Sun Chen grew ever more jealous of Liang, then deposed Liang and established Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Sun's wife was Jun's sister; Sun Chen, ever more hostile to Sun Liang, deposed him and raised Sun Xiu to the throne.

sentences.zh: 永安五年262年，立夫人為皇后。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yong'an (262 CE), he established the lady as empress.
translations.idiomatic: In Yong'an 5 (262) he made Lady Zhu empress.

sentences.zh: 休卒，群臣尊夫人為皇太后，孫皓即位月餘，貶為景皇后。

translations.literal: When Xiu died, the host of ministers honored the lady as empress dowager; a little more than a month after Sun Hao succeeded, she was demoted to Empress Jing.
translations.idiomatic: At Sun Xiu's death the court hailed her as empress dowager; a month after Sun Hao took the throne she was reduced to Empress Jing.

sentences.zh: 稱安定宮。

translations.literal: She was styled the Palace of Anding.
translations.idiomatic: She was given the title Palace of Anding.

sentences.zh: 甘露元年265年七月，見逼薨，合葬定陵。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Ganlu (265 CE), she was forced and died; joint burial at Ding Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Ganlu 1 (265) she was driven to her death and was buried with Sun Xiu at Ding Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 《搜神記》曰：孫峻殺朱主，埋於石子岡。

translations.literal: The Soushen ji states: Sun Jun killed Lady Zhu and buried her at Shizi Hill.
translations.idiomatic: The Soushen ji says Sun Jun killed Lady Zhu and buried her on Shizi Hill.

sentences.zh: 歸命即位，將欲改葬之。

translations.literal: When the Lord Who Surrenders succeeded, he was about to rebury her.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Hao took the throne as Lord Who Surrenders, he meant to give her a proper reburial.

sentences.zh: 塚墓相亞，不可識別，而宮人頗識主亡時所著衣服，乃使兩巫各住一處以伺其靈，使察鑑之，不得相近。

translations.literal: Tombs and graves pressed close together and could not be distinguished; yet palace women fairly well knew the clothes the lady wore at death; therefore he sent two shamans each to dwell in one place to watch for her spirit and have them identify it, not allowing them to approach each other.
translations.idiomatic: The graves lay too close to tell apart, but palace women remembered the clothes Lady Zhu wore at death; Sun Hao posted two shamans at separate spots to watch for her spirit and identify the grave, forbidding them to compare notes.

sentences.zh: 久時，二人俱白：見一女人年可三十餘，上著青錦束頭，紫白袷裳，丹綈絲履，從石子岡上半岡，而以手抑膝長太息，小住須臾，進一塚上便住，徘徊良久，奄然不見。

translations.literal: After a long while both reported: they saw a woman of perhaps thirty-odd years, wearing green brocade head-binding, purple-and-white lined robe, and red silk shoes; from halfway up Shizi Hill she came, pressing her knee with her hand and sighing long; pausing briefly, she advanced to one grave and stopped, pacing for a long while, then suddenly vanished.
translations.idiomatic: After a long wait both reported the same vision: a woman of about thirty in green brocade head-wrap, purple-and-white lined robe, and red silk shoes climbed halfway up Shizi Hill, pressed her knee, sighed, paused at one mound, wandered awhile, and vanished.

sentences.zh: 二人之言，不謀而同，於是開塚，衣服如之。

translations.literal: The two men's words matched without prior agreement; thereupon they opened the grave, and the clothes were as described.
translations.idiomatic: Their accounts matched without collusion; they opened the grave and found the clothes just as described.

sentences.zh: 何姬

translations.literal: Lady He.
translations.idiomatic: Lady He.

sentences.zh: 孫和何姬，丹楊句容人也。

translations.literal: Sun He's Lady He was a native of Jurong in Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Sun He's consort Lady He came from Jurong in Danyang.

sentences.zh: 父遂，本騎士。

translations.literal: Her father Sui was originally a mounted soldier.
translations.idiomatic: Her father He Sui had been a cavalryman.

sentences.zh: 孫權嘗遊幸諸營，而姬觀於道中，權望見異之，命宦者召入，以賜子和。

translations.literal: Sun Quan once toured the various camps, and the lady watched from the road; Quan saw her from afar and thought her unusual, ordered a eunuch to summon her in, and bestowed her on He.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan once inspected the camps; Lady He stood watching from the road. Struck by her looks, he had a eunuch bring her in and gave her to Sun He.

sentences.zh: 生男，權喜。

translations.literal: She bore a son; Quan was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: She bore a son, to Sun Quan's delight.

sentences.zh: 名之曰彭祖，即皓也。

translations.literal: He named him Pengzu—that is, Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan named the boy Pengzu—later Sun Hao.

sentences.zh: 太子和既廢，後為南陽王，居長沙。

translations.literal: After the heir He was deposed, he later became Prince of Nanyang and dwelt at Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: After Sun He lost the heirship he was made Prince of Nanyang and sent to Changsha.

sentences.zh: 孫亮即位，孫峻輔政。

translations.literal: When Sun Liang succeeded, Sun Jun assisted in government.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Liang took the throne, Sun Jun served as regent.

sentences.zh: 峻素媚事全主，全主與和母有隙，遂勸峻徙和居新都，遣使賜死，嫡妃張氏亦自殺。

translations.literal: Jun had long flattered and served the Princess of Quan; the princess and He's mother were at odds, so she urged Jun to move He to Xindu, sent envoys to grant death, and the principal consort Lady Zhang also killed herself.
translations.idiomatic: Jun had long curried favor with Princess Quan, who feuded with Sun He's mother; she talked Jun into exiling Sun He to Xindu and sending orders for his death, and Lady Zhang, his principal consort, killed herself as well.

sentences.zh: 何姬曰：「若皆從死，誰當養孤？」

translations.literal: Lady He said, "If all follow in death, who will raise the orphan?"
translations.idiomatic: Lady He said, "If we all die with him, who will raise these children?"

sentences.zh: 遂拊育皓及其三弟。

translations.literal: Thereupon she nurtured and raised Hao and his three younger brothers.
translations.idiomatic: She then raised Sun Hao and his three younger brothers.

sentences.zh: 皓即位，尊和為昭獻皇帝，《吳錄》曰：皓初尊和為昭獻皇帝，俄改曰文皇帝。

translations.literal: When Hao succeeded, he honored He as Emperor Zhaoxian; the Wu lu states: at first Hao honored He as Emperor Zhaoxian, soon changing it to Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Hao succeeded he canonized Sun He as Emperor Zhaoxian; the Wu lu adds that he soon changed the title to Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 何姬為昭獻皇后，稱昇平宮，月餘，進為皇太后。

translations.literal: Lady He was Empress Zhaoxian, styled the Palace of Shengping; after a little more than a month she was advanced to empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Lady He became Empress Zhaoxian with the title Palace of Shengping, and a month later was raised to empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 封弟洪永平侯，蔣溧陽侯，植宣城侯。

translations.literal: He enfeoffed younger brothers Hong as Marquis of Yongping, Jiang as Marquis of Liyang, and Zhi as Marquis of Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: He enfeoffed her brothers He Hong as Marquis of Yongping, Jiang as Marquis of Liyang, and Zhi as Marquis of Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 洪卒，子邈嗣，為武陵監軍，為晉所殺。

translations.literal: When Hong died, his son Miao succeeded, served as military inspector of Wuling, and was killed by Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Hong died; his heir Miao became inspector of Wuling and was killed by Jin.

sentences.zh: 植官至大司徒。

translations.literal: Zhi reached office as Grand Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi rose to Grand Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 吳末昏亂，何氏驕僭，子弟橫放，百姓患之。

translations.literal: At the end of Wu there was confusion and disorder; the He clan was arrogant and overbearing, sons and younger brothers ran wild, and the common people suffered from it.
translations.idiomatic: In Wu's final years the He clan grew arrogant and their sons ran riot, to the people's misery.

sentences.zh: 故民訛言「皓久死，立者何氏子」云。

translations.literal: Therefore the people spread the saying, "Hao has long been dead; the one enthroned is a son of the He clan."
translations.idiomatic: Hence the rumor that "Sun Hao died long ago—the man on the throne is a He clansman."

sentences.zh: 《江表傳》曰：皓以張布女為美人，有寵，皓問曰：「汝父所在？」

translations.literal: The Jiang biao zhuan states: Hao took Zhang Bu's daughter as a Beauty and favored her; Hao asked, "Where is your father?"
translations.idiomatic: The Jiang biao zhuan says Sun Hao favored Zhang Bu's daughter as a palace lady and asked her, "Where is your father?"

sentences.zh: 答曰：「賊以殺之。」

translations.literal: She answered, "The rebels killed him."
translations.idiomatic: She replied, "The rebels killed him."

sentences.zh: 皓大怒，棒殺之。

translations.literal: Hao was greatly enraged and clubbed her to death.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao flew into a rage and beat her to death.

sentences.zh: 後思其顏色，使巧工刻木作美人形象，恆置座側。

translations.literal: Later, thinking of her looks, he had skilled craftsmen carve wood into a likeness of the beauty and always placed it beside his seat.
translations.idiomatic: Missing her face, he had artisans carve a wooden likeness and kept it at his side.

sentences.zh: 問左右：「布復有女否？」

translations.literal: He asked those at hand, "Does Bu have another daughter?"
translations.idiomatic: He asked his attendants, "Does Zhang Bu have another daughter?"

sentences.zh: 答曰：「布大女適故衛尉馮朝子純。」

translations.literal: They answered, "Bu's elder daughter is married to Chun, son of the former Commandant of the Guards Feng Chao."
translations.idiomatic: They replied, "Zhang Bu's elder daughter had married Chun, son of former Commandant of the Guards Feng Chao."

sentences.zh: 即奪純妻入宮，大有寵，拜為左夫人，晝夜與夫人房宴，不聽朝政，使尚方以金作華燧、步搖、假髻以千數。

translations.literal: He immediately seized Chun's wife into the palace, greatly favored her, appointed her Left Lady, day and night feasted with the lady in the inner chamber, did not attend to court affairs, and had the Directorate of Imperial Manufactures make gold flame-torches, step-shakers, and false coiffures by the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: He seized Chun's wife for the harem, made her Left Lady, and spent day and night feasting with her while neglecting court; he ordered thousands of gold torches, step-shakers, and false coiffures from the imperial workshops.

sentences.zh: 令宮人著以相撲，朝成夕敗，輒出更作，工匠因緣偷盜，府藏為空。

translations.literal: He ordered palace women to wear them in sumo contests; made in the morning and broken by evening, they were constantly replaced; craftsmen took opportunity to steal, and the treasury stores were emptied.
translations.idiomatic: Palace women wore them in mock wrestling bouts that ruined them by evening, so new ones were made constantly while craftsmen stole until the treasury stood empty.

sentences.zh: 會夫人死，皓哀愍思念，葬於苑中，大作塚，使工匠刻柏作木人，內塚中以為兵衛，以金銀珍玩之物送葬，不可稱計。

translations.literal: When the lady died, Hao mourned and longed for her, buried her in the park, built a great tomb, had craftsmen carve cypress into wooden men placed inside the tomb as military guards, and sent gold, silver, and precious curios to the burial beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: When she died Sun Hao mourned extravagantly, burying her in the park with a huge mound, cypress wood soldiers inside the tomb, and incalculable gold, silver, and treasures.

sentences.zh: 已葬之後，皓治喪於內，半年不出。

translations.literal: After the burial, Hao observed mourning within and for half a year did not go out.
translations.idiomatic: After the funeral he kept mourning seclusion for half a year without leaving the palace.

sentences.zh: 國人見葬太奢麗，皆謂皓已死，所葬者是也。

translations.literal: The people of the state, seeing the burial too lavish, all said Hao was already dead and that the one buried was he.
translations.idiomatic: The people, seeing the lavish funeral, decided Sun Hao was dead and someone else had been buried in his place.

sentences.zh: 皓舅子何都顏狀似皓，云都代立。

translations.literal: Hao's maternal nephew He Du resembled Hao in face and form; it was said Du had replaced him on the throne.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew He Du looked like Sun Hao, fueling rumors that Du had taken the throne.

sentences.zh: 臨海太守奚熙信訛言，舉兵欲還誅都，都叔父植時為備海督，擊殺熙，夷三族，訛言乃息，而人心猶疑。

translations.literal: Grand Administrator of Linhai Xi Xi believed the rumor, raised troops wishing to return and execute Du; Du's uncle Zhi was at the time Coastal Defense commander, struck and killed Xi, exterminated three clans, the rumor then ceased, yet hearts still doubted.
translations.idiomatic: Linhai grand administrator Xi Xi believed the rumor and marched to kill He Du; Du's uncle Zhi, coastal defense commander, defeated and killed Xi and wiped out three clans, silencing the rumor though suspicion lingered.

sentences.zh: 滕夫人

translations.literal: Lady Teng.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Teng.

sentences.zh: 孫皓滕夫人，故太常胤之族女也。

translations.literal: Sun Hao's Lady Teng was a clanswoman of the former Grand Master of Ceremonies Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao's empress Lady Teng was a kinswoman of former Grand Master of Ceremonies Teng Yin.

sentences.zh: 胤夷滅，夫人父牧，以疏遠徙邊郡。

translations.literal: When Yin was exterminated, the lady's father Mu, as a distant relation, was banished to a frontier commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After Teng Yin's clan was destroyed, her father Teng Mu was exiled to a frontier commandery as a distant kinsman.

sentences.zh: 孫休即位，大赦，得還，以牧為五官中郎。

translations.literal: When Sun Xiu succeeded, there was a general amnesty; he was able to return, and Mu was made Gentlemen of the Five Offices.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiu's general amnesty let him return; Teng Mu was named a Gentlemen of the Five Offices.

sentences.zh: 皓既封烏程侯，聘牧女為妃。

translations.literal: After Hao was enfeoffed as Marquis of Wucheng, he betrothed Mu's daughter as consort.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Hao was enfeoffed as Marquis of Wucheng, he betrothed Teng Mu's daughter.

sentences.zh: 皓即位，立為皇后，封牧高密侯，拜衛將軍，錄尚書事。

translations.literal: When Hao succeeded, he established her as empress, enfeoffed Mu as Marquis of Gaomi, appointed him Guards General, and recorded Masters of Writing affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At his accession he made her empress, enfeoffed Teng Mu as Marquis of Gaomi, and named him Guards General with oversight of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 後朝士以牧尊戚，頗推令諫爭。

translations.literal: Later court gentlemen, because Mu was an honored affine, largely urged him to remonstrate.
translations.idiomatic: Later courtiers, seeing Teng Mu's rank as empress kin, pressed him to remonstrate with the throne.

sentences.zh: 而夫人寵漸衰，皓滋不悅，皓母何恆左右之。

translations.literal: But the lady's favor gradually declined; Hao grew ever more displeased; Hao's mother He constantly sided with her.
translations.idiomatic: As Lady Teng's favor waned Sun Hao grew angry, while his mother Lady He always sided against her.

sentences.zh: 又太史言，於運歷，后不可易，皓信巫覡，故得不廢，常供養昇平宮。

translations.literal: Moreover the grand astrologer said that in the cycle of fate the empress could not be changed; Hao trusted shamans and sorcerers, therefore she was not deposed, and he regularly maintained offerings at the Palace of Shengping.
translations.idiomatic: Astrologers said the empress could not be changed by fate; Sun Hao trusted diviners, so she kept her title though he maintained rites at the Palace of Shengping instead.

sentences.zh: 牧見遣居蒼梧郡，雖爵位不奪，其實裔也，遂道路憂死。

translations.literal: Mu was seen off to dwell in Cangwu Commandery; although rank was not taken away, in reality he was an exile, and on the road he died of grief.
translations.idiomatic: Teng Mu was sent to Cangwu; though his title remained, he was effectively exiled and died of grief on the road.

sentences.zh: 長秋官僚，備員而已，受朝賀表疏如故。

translations.literal: The Long Autumn officials were names only; receiving court congratulations and memorials continued as before.
translations.idiomatic: The empress's household staff existed in name only; formal congratulations still reached her as before.

sentences.zh: 而皓內諸寵姬，佩皇后璽紱者多矣。

translations.literal: Yet among Hao's favored concubines within, many wore the empress's seal and ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile many of Sun Hao's favorite concubines wore the empress's seal and sash.

sentences.zh: 《江表傳》曰：皓又使黃門備行州郡，科取將吏家女。

translations.literal: The Jiang biao zhuan states: Hao also sent Yellow Gate attendants through the provinces and commanderies to levy and take daughters of generals and clerks' households.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiang biao zhuan adds that Sun Hao sent eunuchs through the provinces to levy daughters of officials.

sentences.zh: 其二千石大臣子女，皆當歲歲言名，年十五六一簡閱，簡閱不中，乃得出嫁。

translations.literal: Daughters of ministers at the two-thousand-bushel rank all had to report their names every year; at ages fifteen or sixteen they were inspected, and only if they failed inspection could they marry out.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers' daughters had to register yearly; at fifteen or sixteen they were inspected, and only those rejected could marry.

sentences.zh: 后宮千數，而採擇無已。

translations.literal: The rear palace numbered in the thousands, yet selection never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The harem held thousands of women, yet the levies never stopped.

sentences.zh: 天紀四年，隨皓遷於洛陽。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianji, she followed Hao in removal to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianji 4 she followed Sun Hao into exile at Luoyang.

translations.literal: Appraisal.
translations.idiomatic: Appraisal.

sentences.zh: 評曰：《易》稱「正家而天下定」。

translations.literal: The appraisal states: The Yi states, "Correcting the family, then all under Heaven is settled."
translations.idiomatic: The appraisal states: The Yi states, "Correcting the family, then all under Heaven is settled."

sentences.zh: 《詩》云：「刑於寡妻，至於兄弟，以御於家邦」。

translations.literal: The Shi jing states: "Model yourself on your few wife, reaching to your brothers, thereby to regulate family and state."
translations.idiomatic: The Shi jing states: "Model yourself on your few wife, reaching to your brothers, thereby to regulate family and state."

sentences.zh: 誠哉，是言也！

translations.literal: Truly, these words!
translations.idiomatic: How true those ancient lines ring!

sentences.zh: 遠觀齊桓，近察孫權，皆有識士之明，傑人之志，而嫡庶不分，閨庭錯亂，遺笑古今，殃流後嗣。

translations.literal: Looking far at Qi Huan, examining near Sun Quan, both had the clarity of wise knights and the ambition of outstanding men, yet legitimate and bastard were not divided, inner chambers were disordered, leaving laughter to ancient and modern, disaster flowing to posterity.
translations.idiomatic: From Duke Huan of Qi down to Sun Quan, both men had a ruler's eye and a hero's drive, yet neither sorted heir from concubine-brood nor kept the women's quarters straight—so they became a byword and their houses paid for it in blood.

sentences.zh: 由是論之，惟以道義為心、平一為主者，然後克免斯累邪！

translations.literal: From this discussing it, only those who take dao and righteousness as heart and equality and unity as master, afterward can overcome this burden!
translations.idiomatic: From this we see: only the ruler who puts moral duty first and keeps heir and concubine lines in fair balance escapes that reckoning!
